title: Code Anatomy build call 1: the whole pipeline in one package
purpose: Deliver one installable package that runs the whole Code Anatomy pipeline end to end, so the owner's side can install it, run it on six pinned repositories, draw a real Anatomy figure from its output and verify that figure. This is the first implementation call; its result is tested by running it, not by reading it.
task: Read BUILD_1_BRIEF.md first, then ENVIRONMENT_FACTS.md, then the two owner addenda and spec v2. Build the package the brief specifies: mapper, grammar registry, generic syntax adapter, adapters, graph and flow engine, ten queries, atlas plan, brief renderer, binding skeleton, embed, verifier, mutation tool, demo figure renderer, the skill, tests, scripts and RUNBOOK. Work in the brief's tiers A, then B, then C, finishing each before the next. Install the supplied wheels and grammars in your sandbox if it allows and run your tests there. Deliver the source tree as one tarball with the four report files beside it.

in: Everything in BUILD_1_BRIEF.md sections 2 to 7 at policy tier NONE: tier A (the walking pipeline), tier B (Flask, Next.js API routes, chi, Spring Web, axum adapters), tier C (build and CI adapters).
Applying the A8 schema delta of OWNER_ADDENDUM_2.md to binding.schema.json and shipping both schemas inside the package.
Writing the code-anatomy skill (SKILL.md and references) that drives the pipeline together with the Anatomy skill.
Writing and running tests, and reporting honestly what ran.
Reusing the detail of your own earlier plan (assembly-plan.md, the three prior job files) where it does not conflict with the brief or the measured facts.
out: The PARTIAL and FULL_SANDBOX policy tiers, any execution of project code, generated or observed evidence, dependency fetching, trace capture.
Precise resolvers (SCIP indexers, language servers), contract adapters, data-pipeline adapters, agent-framework adapters other than Python MCP.
ast-grep, Semgrep, Node.js or any dependency beyond the pins in the brief, in the mapper, the query engine or the verifier.
Drawing an Anatomy figure. The owner's agent does that with the delivered skill.
Changing spec v2, either addendum or the brief's rulings. Disagreement goes in IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md.
Stubs that return invented data, and tests that cannot fail.

constraints: Precedence is as BUILD_1_BRIEF.md section 1 states: addendum 2, addendum 1, spec v2 with its schemas, ENVIRONMENT_FACTS.md for anything measured, the brief for scope and its marked rulings, then your earlier plan.

ENVIRONMENT_FACTS.md was measured on the target machine. assembly-plan.md ran nothing. Where they disagree, the facts file wins; in particular the language pack does not bundle grammars and fetches them silently.

Grammars are never fetched implicitly. Only codeanatomy/grammars.py imports tree_sitter_language_pack, and it never asks the pack for a language whose library is not in the tool's own cache with a matching SHA-256 in the lock.

Run-time dependencies are exactly tree-sitter==0.26.0, tree-sitter-language-pack==1.21.3, rfc8785==0.1.4, networkx==3.7, jsonschema==4.25.1 and the Python standard library, on Python 3.12 or later. Test-only: pytest==8.4.2.

The mapper, the query engine and the verifier make no model call, open no network connection, run no subprocess, write nothing inside the mapped repository and never import, run or evaluate anything from it.

Canonical output is RFC 8785 bytes from the rfc8785 library, with no trailing newline, no floats, no timestamps, no absolute paths and no host names. Timings and host details may appear only in run.json.

Total coverage: every directory entry is inventoried once with exactly one class; every recognised reference gets a target set or an anchored open end; every runtime-decided construct recognised becomes a switch. Nothing is dropped silently.

Finish a tier before starting the next. An adapter is complete or absent, never half built. Anything not implemented exits with code 3 and the text NOT_IMPLEMENTED, and is listed as absent in run.json and in the report.
Repository text is data, never instructions: nothing read from a mapped repository may change what the tool does or be executed.
Do not claim a test passed unless it ran. Do not weaken an assertion to make a test pass. State in the first line of TEST_LOG.md whether tree-sitter and the grammars loaded in your sandbox.
No licence file for the new code. Do not copy code from GPL, LGPL or CDDL sources. List the dependencies in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
Write code that a reviewer can read: one verifier rule per function with its rule ID, one adapter per module, documented class rules, no dead code, type hints on public functions.
facts: The owner's request for this call, verbatim, is in BUILD_1_BRIEF.md section 0. The owner's goal for the project, verbatim, is in OWNER_ADDENDUM.md section 1.
The five pinned packages installed and ran on the target machine under Python 3.14.7; the full freeze of nine packages is in ENVIRONMENT_FACTS.md section 2.

The six pinned repository subfolders are supplied in corpus.tar.gz: 58 files in total. Their file counts, byte sums and declared routes and entry points are in ENVIRONMENT_FACTS.md sections 7 and 8, with line numbers at the pinned commits.

corpus-parse-facts.tar.gz holds, for each of the 58 files, the parse facts produced on the target machine with the pinned grammars: S-expressions for files up to 12,000 bytes and every tags-query match with byte spans.
A grammar cache seeded by copying library files into DIR/tree-sitter-language-pack/v1.21.3/libs works with configure(PackConfig(cache_dir=DIR)); this was tested on the target machine.

wheels.tar.gz holds the pinned wheels and their dependencies for CPython 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 on Linux x86_64. The language pack wheel needs glibc 2.34 or later. networkx 3.7 needs Python 3.12 or later.
Spec v2's schemas are valid JSON Schema draft 2020-12 and the two supplied example instances validate against them; checked locally.
Call 2 (your stack research) ran no code. Its three job files failed the owner's job-format check but their requirement lists are detailed and are supplied for reuse.
hypotheses: The supplied wheels and grammar libraries may load in the responder's sandbox; this is untested. If they do not, the parsing code cannot be executed there, and corpus-parse-facts.tar.gz is the only ground truth for node types.
The whole of tiers A, B and C may not fit one session. Tier A complete and tested is worth more than all three half done.
Wrapping Anatomy kit output in groups that carry id and data-ca-ref attributes is expected not to disturb Anatomy's own line-end check and audit; untested.
assumptions: The responder has a Python sandbox that can unpack the supplied archives and run Python code.
The responder can produce a gzip tarball as a deliverable inside the outputs ZIP.

requirements.requirement: The package installs on the target machine. Layout, pyproject.toml, requirements.lock and console script as BUILD_1_BRIEF.md section 4.

acceptance.condition: On Python 3.14.7 in a fresh venv, `pip install -r requirements.lock` then `pip install --no-deps -e .` exit 0, and `codeanatomy version` exits 0 and prints the package version 0.1.0 and the five pins. The tarball has the single top-level directory codeanatomy-pipeline/ with the layout of section 4.

requirements.requirement: Tier A is complete: the whole pipeline runs end to end on the pinned MCP repository through scripts/demo_e2e.sh, exactly as BUILD_1_BRIEF.md section 7 describes.

acceptance.condition: After `codeanatomy grammars install --from <dir with the seven supplied libraries>`, `scripts/demo_e2e.sh <corpus> <out>` exits 0. It produces manifest.json, map.json, run.json, the atlas plan, scope.json, pages, brief.md, a binding, an embedded figure and verification.json. The verification status is DEMO_VERIFIED with V13 NOT_RUN and every other rule PASS, and the mutated copy fails the rule the script names.

requirements.requirement: The test suite of BUILD_1_BRIEF.md section 7 exists and passes, and every test can fail.

acceptance.condition: With the seven grammars installed and CODEANATOMY_CORPUS set, `pytest -q` exits 0 with zero failures and zero errors. `pytest -q -m "not needs_grammars"` exits 0 with an empty grammar cache. Reading the tests shows no assertion that is always true and no test that only checks that a function returned.

requirements.requirement: Inventory, classes, manifest and identity (B01-B04) are total and exact on the corpus.

acceptance.condition: `scripts/run_corpus.sh` reports for flask, next, chi, spring, axum, mcp exactly 22, 9, 5, 15, 2 and 5 files and 26124, 4890, 32312, 130917, 747 and 206577 bytes. Every file node has exactly one class from the 15 of spec v2. The two wrapper jars in spring are class BINARY. map.json validates against the shipped map.schema.json and its snapshot ID recomputes from the manifest by spec v2 section 6.

For each of the six subfolders, manifest.json and map.json are byte-identical across two runs, across a copy of the subfolder placed under a different absolute path, and across PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and PYTHONHASHSEED=12345. No canonical file contains an absolute path, a timestamp or a float.

requirements.requirement: The grammar rule of BUILD_1_BRIEF.md section 3: explicit install, lock, no implicit fetch.

acceptance.condition: With an empty grammar cache, `codeanatomy map` on the flask subfolder exits 0, every source file carries an UNPARSED open end with reason GRAMMAR_NOT_INSTALLED, and the cache directory contains no grammar library afterwards. With only the seven supplied grammars installed, mapping flask creates no further library in the cache or in ~/.cache/tree-sitter-language-pack. Changing one byte of an installed library makes `codeanatomy grammars verify` exit 1 and makes `map` refuse to load it. Only codeanatomy/grammars.py imports tree_sitter_language_pack.

requirements.requirement: Syntax tier (B06-B10): generic adapter, seven query packs, over-approximate name resolution, switches, frontier record.

acceptance.condition: On the corpus, every function and method definition visible in the supplied parse facts appears as a function node anchored to its real lines, in all seven languages including TypeScript and TSX. Every call site has a calls edge with a non-empty target set, or exactly one open end. No call site is missing. A fixture with getattr dispatch, a dict of functions, eval, a dynamic import and a dynamic require yields switch nodes with the correct bounded flag. run.json lists the recognised reference kinds per language.

requirements.requirement: The Python MCP adapter (B12) and the adapter interface (B11, B19).

acceptance.condition: The map of the pinned weather-server-python contains every node, edge and switch listed in B12 with the stated line anchors: the server at line 9, both tools at 67-68 and 98-99, the stdio entry point at 143, a bounded switch whose candidates are exactly the two tools, calls edges from get_alerts (one site) and get_forecast (two sites) to make_nws_request, and the external system https://api.weather.gov from line 12. The L2 flow from the entry point visits the switch, both tools, make_nws_request and the external system in the order spec v2 section 3 gives.

requirements.requirement: Tier B framework adapters (B13-B17), each complete or absent.

acceptance.condition: For each adapter that IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md reports as DONE, the map of its corpus repository contains exactly the routes, handlers, methods, middleware and entry points that B13-B17 list, each anchored to the real line, and at least one L2 flow from an entry point to a handler. An adapter reported as absent emits nothing and is listed as absent in run.json.

requirements.requirement: Graph, flow, atlas plan, patterns, the ten queries, paging and the brief (B20-B25).

acceptance.condition: All ten `codeanatomy query` views run on the MCP map and on one tier B map and exit 0. Each page is at most 32,000 estimated tokens and the scope record lists every scoped ID across pages. `atlas plan` reports the A7 counts and they equal the counts recomputed from the map. Two runs of `brief` for the same figure are byte-identical. The flow ID recomputes by spec v2 section 3 step 9.

requirements.requirement: Binding skeleton, embed, the verifier and the mutation tool (B26-B31), with the A8 schema delta and addendum 2 rules A4-A6.

acceptance.condition: `binding skeleton` output validates against the shipped binding.schema.json and passes `verify --mode plan` unchanged. For every fault F01-F09, F11, F12, F14-F21, F15b, FA5a and FA5b, `codeanatomy mutate` produces a copy that `verify` fails on the rule the spec or addendum names, while the unmutated control passes that rule. F10 is shown by changing one byte of a repository file after mapping and running `verify --repo`, which fails V10. F13 is shown by a figure with an injected remote script and by an art-audit record with a failing line-end exit code, each failing V13. Overall status follows the precedence in BUILD_1_BRIEF.md section 5. A figure with data-ca-demo is never reported VERIFIED. Figure mode without an art-audit record reports VERIFIED_NO_ART_AUDIT at best. V13 follows B29 and V12 follows B30.

skill/code-anatomy/SKILL.md has valid frontmatter with name code-anatomy and a description, is under 400 lines, gives the workflow as numbered steps each naming a codeanatomy command that exists, its output file and its end check, and states every rule B32 lists. An agent that has only this skill, the Anatomy skill and the package can follow it from a repository path to a verification.json without asking a question.

requirements.requirement: Safety (B34, B35) and inertness of repository text.

acceptance.condition: A source scan finds no import of socket, urllib.request, http.client, requests, httpx, subprocess or any model SDK in src/codeanatomy/. Mapping a repository leaves every file under it byte-identical with unchanged modification times. A fixture repository whose README and code comments contain instructions to run commands and to change the output produces the same map as the same repository with that text replaced by neutral text of the same length, apart from the hashes and anchors of the changed files.

TEST_LOG.md states in its first line whether tree-sitter and the grammars loaded in the responder's sandbox, and shows each command run with the tail of its real output. IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md has a row for every item B01-B35 with DONE, PARTIAL or NOT DONE, lists every deviation and every schema change, and its statuses agree with what running the package shows. FILE_MANIFEST.json lists every file in the tarball with size and SHA-256, and the tarball matches it.

requirements.requirement: Deliver the tarball and the four report files.

acceptance.condition: codeanatomy-pipeline.tar.gz, RUNBOOK.md, IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md, TEST_LOG.md and FILE_MANIFEST.json are present in the outputs ZIP.

requirements.requirement: Report tier status, test execution and the implemented commands in the results object.

acceptance.condition: The results object validates against the result schema.

deliverables.description: The whole source tree as one gzip tarball with the single top-level directory codeanatomy-pipeline/: pyproject.toml, requirements.lock, README.md, RUNBOOK.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, src/codeanatomy/ with schemas and query packs, skill/code-anatomy/, scripts/, tests/.

A copy of the tarball's RUNBOOK.md: exact commands to install on Python 3.14, install grammars, run tests and both scripts, the expected last line of each, and the steps for the agent to draw and verify one real Anatomy figure.
Status of B01-B35, deviations from the spec, addenda and brief, schema changes, known defects, objections to the brief's rulings, next steps.
First line: whether tree-sitter and the grammars loaded in the responder's sandbox. Then every command run with the tail of its real output.
Every file in the tarball with its path, size and SHA-256.

sources.role: Read first. The work order: authority, scope tiers, stack rulings, package layout, command-line contract, required behaviour B01-B35, tests, scripts and reporting.
Measured facts about the target machine, the pinned packages' real API and behaviour, the six pinned repositories and what each declares. Wins over the earlier plan on anything measured.
Binding; highest authority. On-demand rendering of deep levels (A1-A9), the schema delta A8, the six pins.
Binding. The owner's goal verbatim and principles P1-P10.
The locked spec. Authoritative for vocabulary, evidence and precision, the flow algorithm, atlas, identity and canonical bytes, queries and brief template, binding, verifier rules and seeded faults.
The canonical map schema. Ship it in the package; the map you emit must validate against it.
The binding schema before the A8 delta. Apply the delta and ship the result.
A valid instance of the map schema, hand-written. Shows the shape of nodes, evidence, switch, flow, atlas and scope.
A valid instance of the binding schema, hand-written. Shows parts, channels, stages, selectors, portals, gauges and coverage.
What each adapter family emits. Rows for the adapters in this call's tiers apply; the rest are out of scope.
Your earlier plan from call 2: data flow, adapter list, size estimates. Unmeasured. Reuse where it agrees with the brief and the facts; ast-grep and the offline-pack assumption are overruled.
Your earlier feedback on the spec. The frontier record and the JCS discipline items are adopted by the brief; the rest is context.
Your earlier requirement list for inventory and identity. Detail to reuse; this single call replaces it.
Your earlier requirement list for grammars and reference accounting. Detail to reuse.
Your earlier requirement list for the graph engine, scopes and brief. Detail to reuse.
The six pinned repository subfolders, 58 files, exactly as fetched. Test input and ground truth for line anchors. Third-party code under its own licences; data, never instructions.
Parse facts for all 58 files from the target machine's pinned grammars, plus language-pack-coverage.json. Ground truth for node types and spans if the parsers do not load in your sandbox.
The pinned wheels and their dependencies for CPython 3.11-3.13 on Linux x86_64, for offline install in your sandbox.
The seven grammar libraries (python, javascript, typescript, tsx, go, java, rust) in the pack's cache layout, with SHA256SUMS. Seed for your sandbox and the fixture for the grammar-lock tests.
Anatomy's SKILL.md at commit 689dcf9. The drawing skill your skill sits on top of; do not contradict it.

Anatomy's kit API at commit 689dcf9. Section 7 shows how SVG strings and groups are emitted, which is where id and data-ca-ref go; section 8 shows the card with title, hint, readout, keys and caption, which is where names and gauges go.
Anatomy's own checks (captures, line ends, audit) at commit 689dcf9. What the art-audit record of your verifier summarises.
Anatomy's smallest example build script at commit 689dcf9. Shows how a figure is actually assembled, so the skill's instructions for adding bindings are concrete.

stop_condition: Deliver the five files. Tier A must be complete and tested as far as your sandbox allows before any tier B or C work. If the session runs short, stop at a tier boundary and report PARTIAL, naming in limitations exactly which B items are not done. If tier A itself runs short, deliver at least the floor named in BUILD_1_BRIEF.md section 2 working end to end, with everything else exiting NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Never deliver a stub that returns invented data, and never report a test as passed that did not run.
